newsitem.title: USA: Eli Lilly says FDA clears prozac for bulimia.
newsitem.headline: Eli Lilly says FDA clears prozac for bulimia.

text.p: The antidepressant drug Prozac won Food and Drug Administration approval for sale as the first medicine for the eating disorder bulimia nervosa, manufacturer Eli Lilly and Co. said Monday.
The illness strikes more than 1 million Americans a year, almost all of them women, Lilly said.

Bulimia is characterised by recurrent episodes of uncontrolled binge eating followed by some kind of compensatory behaviour, most often purging, which includes self-induced vomiting or misuse of laxatives and diuretics.
Clinical studies have shown that treatment with Prozac leads to a significant reduction in binging and purging episodes, said Freda Lewis-Hall, director of the Lilly Centre for Women's Health.
The most common side effects reported in the clinical trials included insomnia, nausea, anxiety and loss of strength, the Indianapolis-based drug maker said.
Lilly stock rose $3.125 to $78 on the New York Stock Exchange.
Industry analysts said Lilly may not see a huge gain in sales, but said the FDA action was a plus for the company.
"It will help the sales force, give them something new to talk about. It also will keep the drug in the minds of doctors," said Jean Rosenbaum, an analyst at PNC Investment Management & Research.

Prozac is a widely prescribed antidepressant that inspired a best-selling book, "Listening to Prozac". It was approved for treating clinical depression in 1987 and for obsessive-compulsive disorder in 1994.
Lilly said it is estimated that more than 24 million people worldwide, including more than 18 million in the United States, have been treated with Prozac since its introduction.

To date, Prozac has been made available for treating depression in 107 countries and for obsessive-compulsive disorder in 39. The United States is the 34th country in which Prozac has been cleared for treating bulimia.
